column1: # manifest.tsv - how each tracked file becomes a live config on a machine.
# Tab-separated. Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are comments.
# source    path relative to this repo's root, referred to below as $DOTFILES.
#           $DOTFILES is wherever the clone lives - never a hardcoded path.
# strategy  how the target is produced:
#             link         repo owns the target outright (symlink)
#             wrap         target is a stub that sources the repo file, then a
#             include      repo file pulled in via the tool's own include
#             append-once  idempotent marker-delimited block appended; the rest
#                          of the target is left untouched
#             merge-json   jq merge of the tracked key subset into existing JSON
#             never        not installed by this repo; the note says who owns the
#                          target and what overwriting it would break. The source
#                          column is a label only - no repo copy exists, because
#                          a tracked copy of a file we refuse to install only rots
# note       why this strategy, and what breaks if the strategy is wrong or a
# Every install must degrade gracefully: a missing tool may cost a feature, it
# may never break ls, cat, cd, git, or shell startup.
# Section headers (# ---- name ----) are the group names install.sh --only takes.

column4: Every zsh reads ~/.zshenv - interactive, non-interactive, script, agent, CI - so guards that must always apply live here. The eza stdin guard belongs here, not in zshrc: eza >=0.23 reads stdin for paths when stdout is not a TTY and hangs forever with no path argument, and .zshrc is never sourced by an agent or CI shell.

~/.zshrc becomes a stub that sources $DOTFILES/zshrc, then ~/.zshrc.local if it exists. Machine-specific PATH entries, work aliases, and anything secret-adjacent stay in the untracked .local file and out of this public repo.
Repo owns the file. The plugins in vim/plugins.txt must be cloned into ~/.vim/pack/bundle/start/ (vim 8+ native packages); missing ones cost their features silently, nothing errors.
Directory symlink. The BufNewFile autocmds in vimrc read ~/.vim/templates/skeleton.* by absolute path, so the whole directory must resolve, not individual files.

Prompt config only. Nothing breaks when starship is absent because zshrc guards its init behind command -v. Provides the repo-root-relative path display (truncation_length=0 + truncate_to_repo=true) that the agent status lines also want.

Both the tool and the human edit this file, so append a marker-delimited block (# >>> dotfiles managed block >>>) and rewrite only that region. IMPORTANT: ghostty loads BOTH ~/.config/ghostty/config and ~/.config/ghostty/config.ghostty, and config.ghostty is read LAST - verified by setting the same key in both, where config.ghostty won. Keep exactly one of them. A leftover config.ghostty silently overrides this managed block. Ghostty logs an error per unrecognized key, so only append keys the installed version accepts.

Add [include] path = $DOTFILES/gitconfig to a user-owned ~/.gitconfig, and keep identity in ~/.gitconfig.local (also included). A symlink here destroys the machine's user.email, user.signingkey, and any [filter "lfs"] block written by git-lfs install.
Global gitignore. Git ships no default file at this path, so a symlink cannot clobber user content.

Canonical shared instructions. Portable statements only: machine-specific environment claims (which TeX engine, which model runtime, which GPU) belong in an untracked ~/.agents/AGENTS.local.md, because asserting a tool exists on a fresh machine sends agents down dead ends.
Second symlink to the same file so Claude Code reads one source of truth. Point it at ~/.agents/AGENTS.md, not at $DOTFILES, so the repo can move.
Third symlink to the same file for Codex. Same indirection through ~/.agents/AGENTS.md.

Fourth symlink to the same file for OpenCode: its global instructions path is fixed at ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md and it follows neither CLAUDE.md nor ~/.agents/AGENTS.md. Same indirection through ~/.agents/AGENTS.md.
Skills-system design doc: the two layers, the link recipes, and the frontmatter keys each tool honors. Absolute link, same shape as the skills themselves.
Relative symlink ../../.agents/SKILLS.md; the doc sits in the skills dir it describes.
Relative symlink ../../.agents/SKILLS.md; the doc sits in the skills dir it describes.
Personal skill: translate agent-generated prose into plain, direct English.
Personal skill: keep agent-authored code changes minimal, idiomatic, and within scope.
Personal skill: stage selectively, commit, push, refresh the PR body. Commit signing is whatever the machine configures in ~/.gitconfig.local; this repo does not set it.
Personal skill: checkpoint session context to a memory file before a context wipe.
Personal skill: reload a memory file and re-verify it against the codebase.

Personal skill: run Orca multi-agent work through the orcw wrapper (bin/orcw) instead of the raw orchestration CLI. Inert without ~/bin/orcw and a running Orca app; the vendored orchestration skill stays for the commands orcw does not wrap.
Personal skill: propose a PR description update via gh, never write without approval. Needs the gh CLI authenticated.
Forked from superpowers 6.2.0: explore intent, requirements, and design before creative work. Its optional visual companion (scripts/server.cjs) needs node on PATH and silently no-ops without it.
Forked from superpowers 6.2.0: root-cause debugging process before proposing fixes.
Forked from superpowers 6.2.0: run verification and confirm output before claiming done.
Forked from superpowers 6.2.0: turn a spec into a bite-sized, testable implementation plan file.
Forked from superpowers 6.2.0: execute a written plan inline with review checkpoints.
Forked from superpowers 6.2.0: execute a plan via fresh subagent per task with two-stage review; bundles its own code-reviewer.md prompt.
Forked from superpowers 6.2.0: fan independent tasks out to parallel agents.
Forked from superpowers 6.2.0: verify review feedback technically before implementing it.

Vendored snapshot of ayghri/i-have-adhd 0.2.0 (MIT): opt-in /i-have-adhd output shaping for long multi-step sessions. disable-model-invocation and agents/openai.yaml keep it explicit-only in both tools; the upstream always-on hook is deliberately not installed.

Directory symlink. AGENTS.md sends agents to ~/.agents/reference/transcription.md by absolute path, so the directory has to resolve - without this row that pointer is a dead end on every machine. Runbooks only: no machine state, no credentials.

Claude Code writes this file itself (plugin enable/disable, dismissed prompts, marketplace paths), so merge the tracked key subset with jq rather than linking. The statusLine command pipes through jq: without jq on PATH the status line is silently blank.

Codex rewrites this file in place, adding installation-specific marketplace paths, MCP servers, and project trust. Linking or overwriting it drops that state. Treat the repo copy as a reference base and copy keys across by hand.

gh rewrites this file on `gh config set` and on schema migrations, so with a symlink those edits land in the repo working tree - visible in git status, never lost. Credentials stay in the sibling hosts.yml, which is gitignored and never installed.
VS Code writes this file from its own settings UI and extensions add keys to it. A symlink would let the UI edit the repo and reformat or drop keys, so jq-merge the tracked subset instead.

yt-dlp never writes its own config file. The options assume ffmpeg and a node JS runtime; a missing one fails an individual download rather than the shell. Only meaningful with yt-dlp installed (Brewfile.optional).
Create ~/.gnupg with mode 700 first or gpg refuses to use it. Only relevant when gnupg is installed (Brewfile.optional); harmless otherwise.

Docker Desktop rewrites this file from its Settings UI, so merge keys instead of linking. Note builder.gc.defaultKeepStorage is deprecated in favour of a builder.gc.policy array; keep the tracked keys current or Docker warns on start.

zshrc puts ~/bin at the front of PATH, and the script resolves its own symlink chain back to the clone, so the copy on PATH always audits this checkout. It writes nothing to the machine or the repo. git is needed to enumerate tracked files for the leak scan; jq only to verify the merge-json rows.

zshrc puts ~/bin at the front of PATH. Bash launcher that resolves its symlink chain back to the clone and runs lib/orcw.py under uv (falls back to python3). Needs the orca CLI on PATH and the Orca app running; `orcw doctor` reports what the installed Orca version lacks.
zshrc puts ~/bin at the front of PATH. Self-contained bash; override the checkout location with ALTTAB_SRC. Needs full Xcode selected, not just the Command Line Tools.

On a real machine this target is owned by other tools' installers - Homebrew shellenv, container and VM shell hooks, toolchain env snippets - which append to it and rewrite it on upgrade. Overwriting silently removes working integrations. Add the brew shellenv line by hand, or keep it in ~/.zshenv.

Same ownership problem: installer-generated env hooks live here (the uv / rust-toolchain `. $HOME/.local/bin/env` line is exactly one of them) and are regenerated on upgrade. Overwriting silently removes working integrations.

Generated by uv's own installer alongside ~/.local/bin/env.fish and recreated on upgrade. Rerun the uv installer instead of linking; no copy is tracked here (a tracked copy of installer output only rots).
